requirements.title: Defined unary operators occupy the highest precedence layer
requirements.definition: Level-1 expressions are primaries optionally operated on by defined unary operators, and defined unary operators have the highest operator precedence. This precedence statement is structural; defined-operation applicability and interpretation remain dependencies.
requirements.oracle:
Future precedence controls must use user-defined functions with distinctive literal results and must not claim coverage of generic resolution beyond 15.4.3.4.2 and 10.1.6.

requirements.title: A level-1 expression is an optional defined unary operator followed by a primary
requirements.definition: The level-1-expr syntax is either a primary or a defined-unary-op immediately followed by a primary. The operator is prefix and non-repeating in this grammar level unless another primary form introduces parentheses or a lower expression.
requirements.oracle:
Negatives must use well-formed defined-unary-op spellings and valid interfaces so the only defect is the absence of a primary after the first operator.

requirements.title: A defined unary operator is a dotted sequence of letters
requirements.definition: The defined-unary-op spelling is a period, one or more letters, and a period. Digits, underscores, missing dots, and empty names are not part of this syntactic form.

requirements.title: Defined unary operator names are short and not intrinsic or logical-literal spellings
requirements.definition: A defined-unary-op shall not contain more than 63 letters and shall not be the same as any intrinsic-operator or logical-literal-constant. This is a lexical/name restriction independent of whether a matching interface exists.
requirements.oracle:
Length and reserved-spelling negatives must retain R1004 dotted-letter syntax; malformed dots or digits are not C1005 evidence.
